raw_findings.body: NullPointerException is thrown when dereferencing myUser.recoveryCodes, aborting credential enumeration for that user.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime NPE during federated credential enumeration.
raw_findings.impact: NullPointerException is thrown when dereferencing myUser.recoveryCodes, aborting credential enumeration for that user.
raw_findings.root_cause: New getCredentials method omits the null check on the result of getMyUser that sibling methods perform.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a null guard for myUser (return Stream.empty() when null), consistent with isConfiguredFor and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream which already null-check getMyUser.
raw_findings.title: getCredentials override dereferences possibly-null MyUser
raw_findings.trigger: getCredentials(realm, user) is invoked for a user whose translated username is not present in the in-memory users map, so getMyUser(user) returns null.

raw_findings.body: NullPointerException instead of returning false, breaking the null-safe convention used by the surrounding checks.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Potential NPE and inconsistency with established null-safe equals convention.
raw_findings.impact: NullPointerException instead of returning false, breaking the null-safe convention used by the surrounding checks.
raw_findings.root_cause: Introduced condition invokes equals on the untrusted variable rather than the constant.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Invert the comparison to RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE.equals(credentialType) to remain null-safe like the neighboring conditions.
raw_findings.title: Non-null-safe reversed equals in supportsCredentialType
raw_findings.trigger: supportsCredentialType is called with credentialType == null; PASSWORD.equals and isOTPType are null-safe and fall through, reaching credentialType.equals(...).

finding.root_cause: New getCredentials method omits the null check on the result of getMyUser that sibling methods perform.
finding.suggested_fix: Add a null guard for myUser (return Stream.empty() when null), consistent with isConfiguredFor and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream which already null-check getMyUser.
finding.title: getCredentials override dereferences possibly-null MyUser
finding.trigger: getCredentials(realm, user) is invoked for a user whose translated username is not present in the in-memory users map, so getMyUser(user) returns null.
finding.verifier_reason: Patch line R235 shows `if (myUser.recoveryCodes != null)` where myUser is obtained from getMyUser(user) at R232 without null check. getMyUser returns `users.get(translateUserName(...))` which can return null if username not in map. Sibling methods like isConfiguredFor and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream check for null myUser before use. This is a valid NPE bug in test code.

finding.body: NullPointerException instead of returning false, breaking the null-safe convention used by the surrounding checks.
finding.failure_mode: Potential NPE and inconsistency with established null-safe equals convention.
finding.impact: NullPointerException instead of returning false, breaking the null-safe convention used by the surrounding checks.
finding.root_cause: Introduced condition invokes equals on the untrusted variable rather than the constant.
finding.suggested_fix: Invert the comparison to RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE.equals(credentialType) to remain null-safe like the neighboring conditions.
finding.title: Non-null-safe reversed equals in supportsCredentialType
finding.trigger: supportsCredentialType is called with credentialType == null; PASSWORD.equals and isOTPType are null-safe and fall through, reaching credentialType.equals(...).
finding.verifier_reason: Patch line R114 shows `credentialType.equals(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` where credentialType is the method parameter. Prior conditions use constant.equals(variable) pattern which is null-safe. If credentialType is null, PASSWORD.equals and isOTPType return false safely, but credentialType.equals throws NPE. This breaks null-safety convention in test code.
